implemented: Authenticated private options/thread/history/submit/check/cancel/attachment APIs. Current actor, membership, Agent directory and exact resource permissions are checked in the transaction; administrators cannot read another user's private conversations.

Existing configuration revision authority reused. Trusted server-only approved execution mapping is separate from contextual Skill binding. Runtime pins actual full Skill, saved configuration/rules and registered model/budget; friend route/reply field adapters preserve original prompt inputs and validate outputs.

Metadata-only bounded private queue and real existing aiWorker lifecycle integration. Each route/reply stage commits a lease-bound dispatch fence with freshly checked authorization/configuration/model/Skill before a network call outside the transaction.

Per-stage at-most-once dispatch: uncertain provider outcomes are not retried. Expired dispatched turns become unknown; route_ready resumes only reply; reply_ready finishes locally. Lost commit acknowledgements and shutdown do not discard paid durable results.

Private work/coach UI, automatic/explicit contextual Skill, project history, file/image preview and paste, original UUID recovery/check/cancel. Identity or permission loss clears private content; intentional Agent switching warns about dirty drafts.
Full candidate rules display without automatic application. Existing configuration editor remains the single rule authority; direct proposal confirmation is explicitly unavailable in this slice.

Use exact thread resource permissions; reject the complete thread list when policy disallows an included thread. Membership/user/workspace revocation maps to FORBIDDEN so the UI clears private state.
Allow the full legal 128KiB configuration body plus its immutable snapshot envelope; retain the original configuration limit.

Preserve paid ready results across shutdown/heartbeat failures and ambiguous result/finish acknowledgements. Current authorization is still required, but a later model/config edit cannot erase an already-paid frozen reply.
Keep logical/context hashes distinct from actual strict provider payload hash, validating both receipt identity and durable stage result.
